neighbours.label: 'what' as a free relative ('the thing that') after a verb or preposition (in what is known as, carry out what was), not interrogative, exclamative or embedded-question 'what'
fire: The fire destroyed what was left of the old farmhouse.
The talks ended in what both sides called a fair compromise.
Rising seas are producing what experts describe as a slow disaster.
The village sits on what used to be the bed of a lake.
She spent her savings on what turned out to be a fake painting.
The council approved what many saw as a reckless budget.
They walked for hours through what looked like an endless forest.
He finally admitted to what had happened that night.
quiet: What was left of the old farmhouse after the fire?
Both sides asked what a fair compromise would look like.
Experts wonder what the rising seas will do to the coast.
What a beautiful lake this used to be!
She never knew what the painting was really worth.
What did the council decide about the budget?
They walked for hours, not sure what forest they were in.
Nobody asked him what had happened that night.

predictions: fire 0.4-0.7 on ' what' after a verb/preposition meaning 'that which'; questions, exclamations and 'know what' below 0.1
